benchmark_context.price_basis: ESTIMATE, and the caveat travels with the number rather than sitting in a footnote. The frozen pricing snapshot returns None for google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it (it is unlisted: no exact rate and no floor), and a scan of all 129 registry entries finds NO published row on any DiffusionGemma base at all - the page's openjev-razorback16 is the same model but a different submitter and carries no v1.6 score - so there was no precedent to copy. The reference used is google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, USD 0.09 per 1M input and USD 0.30 per 1M output: the identically sized and identically shaped publicly hosted Gemma 4 26B-A4B sibling of the unlisted diffusion checkpoint, a closer sibling than the one run 54 had to use for gemma-4-12B-it. x this row's own measured tokens. THE CAVEAT: a token-priced cost axis charges this row as though it ran one forward pass, when the author's own documentation denoises a 256-position canvas for up to 48 adaptive steps per question. The Cost axis therefore UNDERSTATES this configuration's compute, by construction and not by accident; the measured per-question denoising_steps are kept in the raw so the understatement is quantifiable. Estimated, not charged

latency_context.hardware_runtime: measured 2026-10-06 on the live v1.6.0/v1.6.1 pool. github.com/Hangzhi/diffusion-jev-sglang@d61f0a9c0c9b6d78631aa250125dc4b20e9ea0a2 serving google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it@f7f5b7f5fa82ffc52addd066915886d497f5517b on SGLang@ef90bf677e4e6b280bf796f1c5f4ef0f05dda27f (their open PR 34061) with their own version-checked readout and context-admission patch. Built from THEIR OWN tested container recipe (deployment/modal_app.py + deployment/gemma-requirements.txt), which their doc names as the recipe to use; their `engine` extra and top-level Dockerfile target the older LLaDA deployment and their doc says plainly not to use them as a DiffusionGemma installer, so they were not used. SGLang is a pure-python install imported through PYTHONPATH, no source compile. Served with their own scripts/launch_diffusiongemma.py: native Gemma4Renoise, a 256-position canvas, up to 48 adaptive denoising steps, seed 42, thinking disabled, 8,192-token context, Triton attention, no CUDA graphs, no prefix cache, T=1 softmax over the options offered - their configuration, unchanged, on one H100 80 GB (Lium) against the A100 80 GB they tested. THE AUTHOR'S OWN STATEMENT, CARRIED UNSOFTENED: these are self-conditioned denoiser scores, NOT independent masked-token likelihoods and NOT calibrated probabilities of correctness; this is not a one-forward-pass or zero-generation method. There are no new trained weights - it is an inference configuration over Google's unchanged checkpoint. A format mismatch returns their own HTTP 503 and is recorded invalid, the same way for everyone. Latency axis uses the standard self-hosted x2 + 0.15 s adjustment. add-requests run 55, GitHub #30

latency_context.context: The author's own README Quickstart install line (pip install -e '.[dev]') at code pin github.com/devops-thiago/class-one@6cca132b and their own serve line (uvicorn classone.server.app:app); their server registers POST /v1/systemone itself, so the request and answer shapes are theirs. CLASSONE_BASE_MODEL was pointed at the LOCAL PINNED SNAPSHOT DIRECTORY, which their own code accepts, so the revision cannot drift to main and classone_heads.pt resolves locally with no request-time hub fetch. Their hard-coded MAX_TOKENS_PER_REQUEST = 8192 refuses longer prompts with HTTP 400; those items are recorded as invalid, the same way for every system. ONE documented mapping of ours and the only one: their server keys score probabilities '1'..'n' while JevBench's canonical keys are '0'..'n-1', so run 58's byte-identical ClassOneReindexAdapter relabels score keys k -> k-1 by calling the unchanged vendored typesafe adapter's own run(), and an item whose key set is not exactly {'1'..'n'} is REFUSED rather than rescored on a guess; choice and noul are untouched. The two already-published ClassOne rows carry exactly this treatment. evaluator-owned Lium RTX 5090 32 GB pod (pod calm-wolf-31, USD 0.72/h; Brasov, Romania, EU by the RIPE whois of its public IP, receipt r90/receipts/POD-IP-WHOIS-R90.txt); pod-level iptables egress cut installed, verified and TIMESTAMPED pod-side (logs/EGRESS-CUT-R90.log) BEFORE the sealed input was uploaded, so the ordering is provable from pod evidence and not only from the session transcript; HF/transformers offline, no credentials in the environment, one decision per request, no batching, no retry. The five rows ran strictly one at a time on the one card, each server started with setsid and stopped by its exact process group with a card-free check in between.

ONE documented mapping of ours and the only one: their server keys score probabilities '1'..'n' while JevBench's canonical keys are '0'..'n-1', so run 58's byte-identical ClassOneReindexAdapter relabels score keys k -> k-1 by calling the unchanged vendored typesafe adapter's own run(), and an item whose key set is not exactly {'1'..'n'} is REFUSED rather than rescored on a guess; choice and noul are untouched. latency_context.context: Sandy, the evaluator's own shared CPU host (AMD Ryzen 5 3600, 6 cores / 12 threads, Zen 2, AVX2), NOT a dedicated machine: other jobs ran beside it and the 1-minute load average was logged every 60 s into logs/CONDITIONS-julia-1.jsonl (11 samples, 10.87-13.78, mean 12.5). The author ships NO server, so the HTTP surface is OURS: r107/src/julia_shim_r107.py, a pure transport that makes no mapping decision, because the author's own julia.typed.predict_typed already speaks JevBench's typed-question shape exactly (choice keyed by the item's own criteria keys, score keyed '0'..'n-1' with score = sum(i*p_i), noul = p(true)). Engine built with the author's own inference-policy.json (max_length 8192, head_length 512, strict_encoding true), torch backend, device cpu, float32 (their julia_config weight_dtype), thread count left at their own default of 4 - all four read back from the run's own /health rather than asserted. Run inside a loopback-only network namespace whose outbound probe failed as required, offline (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1), credential-free, nice 5, in a systemd scope with MemoryMax=8G and no swap. Speed is therefore a loaded-shared-CPU figure and a lower bound for this model on a dedicated core or a GPU; the standard self-hosted x2 + 0.15 s adjustment is applied on top and the raw p50/p95 are kept. Measured for this release on the frozen v1.6-regular-20261012 self-hosted input (sha256 dfd36720...) under CoS deputy decision #18209, which admitted this row only after an independent source review and a synthetic-only smoke, both of which were met in that order before the first sealed item. DISCLOSED: the author's own strict_encoding policy REFUSES rather than truncates, so 17 of the 1,500 items (15 over their lossless context budget, 2 with an option above their 48-token option contract) are honest item-level misses recorded as HTTP 422 - predicted exactly, class split included, before the run.
